raw_response:
I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I look over the road and see what the better fields are doing. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard, because if the crop goes hungry the yield is gone, and that hurts more than spending a bit extra. My land is 12 mu, and with wheat-maize as the main pattern, I will keep most of the land in that rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I will put 8 mu into wheat-maize and 4 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use a good improved seed like the people around me use, put enough base fertilizer in, then topdress when the seedlings stand strong. With well water, I will give wheat three irrigations if the year is normal. After wheat harvest, I will rush into maize on the same 8 mu. Maize must not miss time, so I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, and water it two times if rain is not enough. Cotton takes more watching by hand, more spraying too, but if I keep only 4 mu I can still manage it. I will not chase fancy new methods. I will do what I know, with a little care on seed and water, and keep money aside for pesticide and hired help when the busy days come.
